narrative.overview:
The store's Machuca-style cement-tile floor is the system. Every panel is a square tile of warm limewash (tile) set into a lighter mortar ground (grout), separated by a visible 4px grout joint and finished with one-pixel rules. An oxblood rail runs down the left like the store's painted wainscot. The floor pattern itself, an ochre-slate-oxblood four-fold medallion, is drawn once in `TileMotif.jsx` and in the `--motif` data URI, and is cropped two ways: a quarter-disc in the corner of ordinary tiles, and the full repeat on exactly one element per screen.

Density is a working back office's: compact tables, 44px controls, clear labels in the brief's own words. Colour is pigment, not decoration: oxblood is the store's voice and primary action, ochre marks the live or selected thing (today, focus, the active icon), slate carries data. Depth is almost entirely grout and tone; shadows exist only for things that float above the floor (the pop-up and the phone drawer).

The system refuses the generic white-card admin template: no floating white cards on gray, no soft drop shadows on panels, no rounded 12px pills.
keyCharacteristics: Square tiles on a 4px grout joint; corners never past 3px.
One full-pattern element per screen; every other tile shows only the quarter-motif corner.
Oxblood rail and primary action; ochre for the live thing; slate for data.
One grotesque (Schibsted Grotesk, self-hosted variable 400–900), heavy for figures.
Flat floor; shadow only on floating layers.

rules.name: The Pigment Roles Rule
rules.body: Oxblood speaks for the store and the primary action; ochre marks the one live or selected thing; slate carries data. Never swap roles: a slate button or an ochre primary action is off-system.

rules.name: The No-White-Card Rule
rules.body: Panels are tile (`#f3efe7`) on a grout joint, never white cards on gray. White is reserved for input wells and hover lift.

rules.name: The Lining Figures Rule
rules.body: Money and counts use the grotesque's own proportional lining figures (`font-variant-numeric: lining-nums`), never tabular. Right-alignment in table `num` columns does the aligning; the figures keep their natural widths.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Schibsted Grotesk at varied weight is the whole type system. Hierarchy comes from weight and size, not from a second face.

rules.name: The Flat Floor Rule
rules.body: Tiles, panels and tables never carry a drop shadow. If it sits on the floor, it is separated by grout; only the modal and the drawer lift.

rules.name: The One Patterned Tile Rule
rules.body: Exactly one element per screen carries the full pattern: the dashboard's Today's sales tile (pattern field on its right 30%), or a `.patterned` band (a 40px pattern strip under a 3px oxblood rule along the top of the page's main tile: the registration form, user account form, POS cart, report results tile (the band sits on a wrapper around a borderless table well, so the pattern stays outside the horizontal scroll), login tile at 96px, payroll's Net pay cell at 26px). A patterned element drops its quarter corner. A second full pattern on a screen is off-system.

rules.name: The Quarter Corner Rule
rules.body: Every other panel, card, stat tile and POS product shows the quarter-motif in its top-right corner, and clears it with 44px of top padding so the heading sits beneath the corner rather than beside it.

dos: **Do** separate tiles with the 4px grout joint (line-colour gap and border), not with spacing and shadow.
**Do** give every screen exactly one full-pattern element: the dashboard tile field or one `.patterned` band on the page's main tile.
**Do** put the quarter-motif corner on every other panel, card, stat tile and product, and give the panel 44px of top padding to clear it.
**Do** keep oxblood for the rail and primary action, ochre for today, focus and the selected item, slate for data.
**Do** set money and counts heavy (800) with proportional lining figures, right-aligned in tables.
**Do** keep controls at 44px minimum for touch.
**Do** respect reduced motion: all animation and transition are removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** round corners past 3px on tiles, buttons, inputs or nav.
**Don't** put a drop shadow on any tile, panel or table; only the modal and drawer lift.
**Don't** use plain white as a panel surface; white is for input wells and hover lift.
**Don't** show the full pattern twice on one screen, or add a quarter corner to the patterned element.
